{{c|{{xx-larger|THE EPISTLE OF}}}}
{{c|{{x-larger|PAVL THE APOSTLE}}}}
{{c|{{larger|TO THE ROMANES.}}}}

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. I.}}}}}}

{{c|''The foundation of his Apostleship being laid, 8 he highly commendeth the Romanes, and protesteth his affection tovvardes them. and so comming to the matter, saith, our Christian Catholike doctrine (that teacheth al to beleeue) to be the vvay to saluation: 18 because the Gentiles (first of al) could not be saued by their Philosophie, whereby they knew God, for so much as they did not serue him, but Idols: he therfore iustly permitting them to fall into al kind of most damnable sinne.''}} {{dropinitial|P|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial P, flowers and foliage.png|imgsize=230px|fl={{verse|chapter=1|verse=1}}}}AVL {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 13, 2.''}}* the seruant of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, called to be an Apostle, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle vpō Christmas eue. · Act. 13, 2.}}∷ separated into the Gospel of God, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=2}}† vvhich before he had promised by his Prophets in the holy Scriptures, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=3}}† of his sonne, (vvho vvas made to him of the seede of Dauid according to the flesh, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=4}}† vvho vvas predestinate the sonne of God in povver, according to the spirit of sanctification, by the resurrectiō of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} from the dead, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=5}}† by vvhom vve haue receiued grace and Apostleship {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Faith must not be subiect to sense, reason, arguing or vnderstāding, but must cōmaund & be obeied in humilitie and simplicitie.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως''.}}∷ for obedience to the faith {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Augustine vseth this place and the like agaĩst Heretikes, which would draw the common Catholike faith of al natiōs, to some certaine countries or corners of the vvorld. ''Aug. ep. 161''.}}∷ in al Nations for the name of him, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6}}† among vvhom are you also the called of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}:)⊣ {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7}}† to al that are at Rome the beloued of God, called to be saincts. {{sup|‖}} Grace to you and peace from God our father, and our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=8}}† First I giue thankes to my God through {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} for al you, because {{sup|‖}} your faith is renoumed in the vvhole world. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=9}}† For God is my vvitnes, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ᾧ λατρεύω''.}}∷ vvhom I {{sup|‖}} serue in my spirit in the Gospel of his Sonne, that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He praieth without intermission that omitteth no day certaine times of praier. ''Aug. heres. 57''.}}∷ vvithout intermission I make {{sup|‖}} a memorie of you {{verse|chapter=1|verse=10}}† alvvaies in my praiers, beseeching, if by any meanes I may sometime at the length haue a prosperous iourney by the vvil of God, to come vnto you.<noinclude>{{rh|||For}}</noinclude>
